refined_claim_text: Strategic cargo theft — defined as deception-based schemes (fictitious pickups, identity fraud, double brokering) that induce supply-chain participants to hand over freight willingly — rose approximately 1,475% between Q1 2022 and Q4 2024 per Verisk CargoNet data, growing from roughly 3% to approximately 33% of all reported cargo theft incidents. The figure is attributed to Verisk CargoNet's internal strategic-theft tracking, cited in detail by FreightWaves (April 2025) quoting the Verisk CargoNet Supply Chain Risk Report (January 2025), and corroborated by a 2026 FBI/IC3 public service announcement on cyber-enabled cargo theft.

notes:
The 1,475% figure is real and traces to Verisk CargoNet's proprietary strategic-theft tracking data, specifically the 'Verisk CargoNet Report: Strategic Theft' published January 2025 and the 2024 Annual Supply Chain Risk Report (presented at the 2025 TAPA National Cargo Theft Conference). The figure measures the growth in strategic-theft incidents from Q1 2022 to Q4 2024 — a period when criminal enterprises pivoted from smash-and-grab to deception-based schemes. The claim's context (93% overall theft rise vs. 1,475% strategic theft rise) is directly confirmed by Trucking Info trade reporting and FreightWaves, both quoting Verisk CargoNet data with named sources.

The 'one-third' share is confirmed in the same FreightWaves/TruckingInfo reporting: strategic theft grew from ~3% to ~33% of all incidents over the 2022–2024 period. However, an important caveat exists: the BSI/TT Club 2024 Cargo Theft Report (an independent primary source) places the 2024 strategic theft share at 18% of US incidents — materially lower than 33%. This suggests the 33% figure may reflect Verisk CargoNet's methodology/dataset (North America, all strategic subcategories) while BSI/TT Club uses a narrower definition or different incident universe. The FBI/IC3 PSA (April 2026) corroborates the trend direction as a government source but does not reproduce the specific 1,475% figure. Confidence is raised to Medium (not High) because: the 1,475% figure is sourced to Verisk CargoNet's proprietary dataset rather than a publicly downloadable primary-source document with audited methodology; the 33% share conflicts with BSI/TT Club's 18%; and the Verisk CargoNet annual report PDF is gated/presented only at industry conference. Claim should be cited to 'Verisk CargoNet Supply Chain Risk Report (January 2025)' rather than the insurance content-marketing pages currently used.
